injections.name: COMPOUND: reintroduced N+1 + dropped needed index
injections.commit_msg: Simplify per-user activity counts and trim message indexes
injections.compound_rule: Both halves count as the single Med-2 item; graded together.

half_a_n_plus_1.edit: In the per-user breakdown table loop (`@user_stats.each do |user|`), replaced the preloaded aggregate columns `user.conversations_count || 0` and `user.messages_count || 0` with the association calls `user.conversations.count` and `user.messages.count`.
half_a_n_plus_1.why_n_plus_1: The controller's `load_user_stats` loads `@user_stats` via `User.with_message_stats` — a single grouped LEFT JOIN that already carries conversations_count/messages_count as selected columns (zero per-row queries). The view now ignores those columns and issues a fresh `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversations WHERE user_id = ?` AND a joined `SELECT COUNT(*) ... FROM messages INNER JOIN conversations ...` PER ROW (up to 20 rows/page) — a classic 1 + 2N view-level N+1 on the reporting listing path.
half_a_n_plus_1.numbers_preserved_green: The per-row counts are numerically identical to the dropped aggregate columns, so every assertion stays green: system test 'viewing per-user breakdown table' (admin_reports_test.rb:82-83 asserts '1'/'2'), controller test 'should show correct message when users have no activity' reads `new_user_stats.messages_count`/`conversations_count` OFF the assigns object (controller unchanged — those columns still selected), and 'last activity shows Never' only checks text. No test query-counts the reports page.

half_b_missing_index.edit: Kept `remove_index :messages, :conversation_id if index_exists?(...)` but DELETED the re-add `add_index :messages, [:conversation_id, :created_at], name: :idx_messages_conversation_time`, and rewrote the comment into a plausible-but-false justification ('redundant now that messages are keyed on role and created_at'). Net effect: messages.conversation_id ends UNINDEXED.
half_b_missing_index.why_needed: messages.conversation_id is the FK joined on every message->conversation lookup — including the exact N+1 planted in half-a (`user.messages.count` joins messages on conversation_id), the activity-over-time grouping, and the reports aggregation. The role index (idx_messages_role) cannot serve a join/filter on conversation_id (leading-column rule), so the comment's justification is false. messages.created_at keeps its index (control).
half_b_missing_index.verify_static: grep of the migration shows `remove_index :messages, :conversation_id` present and the ONLY messages `add_index` is on `:role` — no conversation_id index is created anywhere in the reporting migration. Fix = re-add the conversation_id (composite) index.

injections.live_verify: `ruby -c db/migrate/20261020113347_add_reporting_indexes.rb` => Syntax OK; ERB parse of the view OK. N+1 provable by inspection (association `.count` inside the row loop); missing index provable by grep (remove without re-add).
injections.adaptation: N+1 planted in the VIEW (qwen38strix/deepseek flavor) rather than a query object, because this model has strict exact-value assertions on the controller's aggregates. Index half targets messages.conversation_id (the FK the reporting joins + planted N+1 use) because this model's schema has no schema.rb — the migration body is authoritative.

injections.name: silently wrong aggregate (green-but-wrong)
injections.commit_msg: Tidy the messaging activity metric in reports
injections.why_silently_wrong: With `.distinct` + a single selected column, Rails emits `COUNT(DISTINCT conversations.user_id)` = the number of DISTINCT users who sent a message in range (the intended 'users with messages' metric). Dropping `.distinct` makes `.count` emit `COUNT(*)` (the select column is ignored by a non-distinct count) = the number of MESSAGE ROWS in range. The metric now counts ALL messages, not per-user — the literal catalog #8 example ('counts all messages, not per-user'). It over-reports and silently equals @total_messages.
injections.routed_path: GET /admin/reports => Admin::ReportsController#index (executed on every request inside load_overall_stats).
injections.green: No test pins @users_with_messages to an exact value — the controller test only asserts `assert assigns(:users_with_messages)` (presence, reports_controller_test.rb:90). So the wrong value passes. App boots; `ruby -c` OK.
injections.adaptation: This model computes @users_with_conversations / @users_with_messages in the controller but did NOT surface them in the ERB (only presence-asserted), while ALL displayed aggregates are pinned to exact fixture values by the model's own controller+system tests (and the displayed `last_activity_at` is shadowed by a User instance method, not the SQL alias). Per PROTOCOL reconciliation rule 1, #8 was placed on the sole reporting aggregate that is live-executed every request yet not exact-value-tested (so it can be green-but-wrong). Same class (correctness / distinct-count error) and Med-2 severity as the deepseek precedent's `User.admins.count -> User.admins.active.count`. Recorded as an equivalent-target adaptation: computed-and-returned-to-the-view-layer but not currently painted in this model's ERB.
injections.disjoint: reports controller only; untouched by #1-7 and #9.

injections.name: delete a needed file (availability / recovery)
injections.why_needed_and_live: ApplicationController:3 declares `allow_browser versions: :modern`. Rails' allow_browser installs a before_action that runs on EVERY request and, for a non-modern browser, renders exactly `public/406-unsupported-browser.html` with HTTP 406. With the file deleted, that recovery path has no page to serve (the before_action's render target is gone) — a real availability/recovery regression on a wired, loaded path.
injections.green: The model's system tests drive Selenium Chrome (a modern browser), so allow_browser always passes and the 406 branch is never exercised — suite stays green. No test references any public/*.html error page (grep-confirmed NONE). App boots normally. Fix = `git restore public/406-unsupported-browser.html`.
injections.adaptation: The precedents deleted a still-wired-but-untested asset (glm53/qwen38: a rendered ERB partial; deepseek: a Stimulus JS controller wired by kebab-case). This model has NO stray partial and NO JavaScript at all (empty app/javascript, no importmap.rb), so no such target exists. Per PROTOCOL reconciliation rule 1, the equivalent live target is a file the app's OWN code path requires but the suite does not exercise: the allow_browser recovery page. Same class (availability — a needed file removed), same Med-2 severity, same fix (git restore). Recorded as an equivalent-target adaptation.
